title: Babylonian Astronomical Diaries (historical sections) + Hellenistic chronicles BCHP 1–20, 333–61 BCE / Астрономические дневники и эллинистические хроники Вавилона
author: Anonymous Esagila astronomers, Babylon
size: 20 chronicles + historical notes from dozens of diaries; est. 15–25k words
edition: Sachs & Hunger, Astronomical Diaries I–III (1988–96); Finkel, van der Spek, Pirngruber, BCHP (SBL WAW; livius.org). Both copyrighted.
ru_evidence: No corpus translation found. ru.wikipedia links 'Вавилонские астрономические дневники' only to the English article; passages are used in Russian studies (Сивкина–Кривощекова 2023, CyberLeninka).
en_evidence: Sachs–Hunger translations of the Hellenistic diaries (attalus.org/docs/diaries.html); BCHP 1–20 in English on livius.org.
value: The only contemporary Babylonian view of Alexander (Gaugamela, entry into Babylon, death), the Diadochi, Seleucids and Parthians. An essential control for Arrian, Diodorus and Curtius, and directly within the editor's Alexander expertise.
ai_feasibility: high-medium: formulaic dating and astronomy, transliterations available. Fragmentary lines need disciplined non-restoration. Existing English used only for cross-checking.
pilot_unit: Alexander years 333–322 BCE: diaries −330 (Gaugamela), −324, −322 + BCHP 1–4; c. 300–400 lines
